name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed and ECB rises priced; yen near 160
summary: Markets price December rate rises by the Fed and ECB; Japan warns on the yen near 160 but has not intervened
state: As of 18 Nov, markets priced a 98% chance of a 25bp Fed rise on 9 Dec and a 91% chance of an ECB rise on 17 Dec (Trading Economics, citing LSEG). The yen's fall stopped just short of 160 per dollar on 12 Nov after Japan's finance minister Katayama warned of one-sided moves and said Tokyo would coordinate with the US Treasury (FXStreet; investingLive). No intervention, emergency move or challenge to a central-bank head was found as of 23 Nov, so this remains a stagflationary dilemma at Watch.
for_you: Borrowing costs in the US and euro area are expected to rise again in December, which tends to feed through to mortgage and loan rates over the following months.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma with hikes priced = Watch; no emergency move or intervention (Alert)

sources.title: Trading Economics — French bond yields (news stream incl. 18 Nov rate pricing)
FXStreet — Japanese Yen decline halts a few pips shy of 160.00 as intervention risks grow

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
